pulse.text: **xAI shipped Grok 4.6 today**, closing out the two-week wait inside Musk's stated window with a 500K context, $2/$6 pricing and an **Artificial Analysis Index of 61** that ties GPT-5.6 Sol and puts it third on the board behind Claude Opus 5 (63) and Claude Fable 5 (62). It is a post-training release, not a scale-up: the same ~1.5T V9 foundation as Grok 4.5, with heavier SFT and RL lifting **DeepSWE v1.1 to 65.9% from 54%** and Terminal-Bench v3.0 to 26% from 15.7% -- and still no model card. Markets moved with it: xAI's year-end best-model leg climbed to 7.6% from 5.1% and Grok 5 now reads 34% before November, while Anthropic holds 67% for year-end, 84% for September and 94% for August. Elsewhere **Google's next Gemini Pro jumped to 55% by Aug 31 from 44%** even as the Aug 14 leg collapsed to 2%, Astra firmed to 79% by Sep 30, and Polymarket's 1520+ Arena ceiling bounced to 59% after a two-sweep slide. The business story stayed on plumbing: OpenAI closed a **$7 billion employee share sale at an $852 billion valuation** ahead of a possible IPO, and Nvidia lined up six asset managers behind a $500 billion push to finance compute like real estate.
